verified_properties: Pinned real MPC-TLS runs against the localhost HTTPS fixture via the native worker, with independently configured verifier origin/root/disclosure/commitment policy. This is not ordinary prefetched HTTPS plus a local hash.

The exact upstream SHA256 commitment construction and random blinder remain upstream-owned. Finite ranges, algorithm, ordering, selected-byte budgets and authenticated TLS lengths are preserved across Rust/C++ FTN2; FTN1 default path continues passing the existing regression suite.

Verifier receives commitments and the selected public transcript ranges, with no openings. Prover receives only explicitly selected openings. Actual commitment/opening equality and hidden-response opening checks pass.

The application fixture signs the entire evidence with its domain/context before invoking the guarded opening path; changed domain/context/signer/origin/length/direction/translated ranges refuse that path. This is an application gate demonstration in one local test harness, not a separate buyer delivery protocol or FairSwap guarantee.

Exact typed failures are asserted for changed bytes/blinder/hash, short or invalid-index opening, unsupported format/pin, invalid/empty/out-of-bounds ranges, enum, duplicates and retained capacities. Rust checks exact policies and private input truncation/suffix/tampering; bounded Raw rejects unknown and narrowing enum representations.

New checker lifetime tests pass active and pre-start cancellation, duplicate/overload, live deadline, lazy operation after shutdown, stopped admission, rogue transport request and no residual child process. The existing lifecycle/backpressure/reaping suite passes.

Canonical evidence and private openings persist separately and are revalidated in a fresh host process. This proves process-restart recovery for the fixture, not filesystem power-loss durability or independent TLS provenance from an untrusted file.
Both fresh installed leaf and plugin consumers use installed modules/archives and the installed worker; copied files are only test-owned fixture/evidence helpers.
